title: Peter Laird and David Choe on TMNT #12 — Cartoonist Kayfabe
summary: Ed Piskor and Jim Rugg host Peter Laird and David Choe for a page-by-page discussion of Laird's solo Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #12 and Choe's 1999 Xeric Grant for Slow Jams. Choe thanks Laird for a career-changing grant; Laird describes the Xeric Foundation as a structured response to overwhelming requests after sudden wealth. Their money discussion moves from former property, motorcycles, cars, toys and a doomsday bunker toward giving money and rare art away while alive, with all prices, charity and ownership claims kept as attributed memories rather than audited records. Laird says he and Kevin Eastman needed solo issues after licensing stress made collaboration difficult, explicitly denying fistfights. The page analysis covers Dr. Ph. Martin's dyes, Prismacolor, Duoshade, airbrush, Steve Lavigne lettering, wilderness texture, Barry Windsor-Smith, realistic toy-gun reference, negative space, silent pages, off-panel violence, visual pacing, Ryan Brown, Stephen R. Bissette and conservation damage caused by stacked tone sheets. Choe asks about April O'Neil's ethnicity; Laird answers only for his own conception, withholds inference about Eastman's intent and traces the name to Eastman's private former girlfriend. Cold War/militia fiction opens into Choe's 1992 Los Angeles unrest, conflict-zone travel and bunker fear, then a later distinction between merely surviving and living well. Weapon stories, graphic violence, racialized/sexual jokes, private property/family details, health self-report, nuclear imagery and fatalistic rhetoric remain uncensored but separately restricted from operational or neutral metadata. The issue ends with family/art history, critical fan letters, Michael Murphy's Steve Murphy/Michael Zulli naming origin and The Puma Blues. Choe's Kayfabe Con and joint-comic ideas are jokes, not announcements. Two house ads are separated. Four public participants are known at episode level, but captions contain zero publisher prefixes, so named line-level turns remain withheld.
